subject: Request: one-time credit for staggered feature rollout (AcmePay)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: one-time credit for staggered feature rollout (AcmePay)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap: AcmePay plans to ship embeddings-based fraud scoring in a two-phase rollout (backend first, frontend widgets later). Your team is landing the backend integration this month but the frontend rollout is delayed by an additional 8 weeks due to QA scheduling. That mismatch increases your near-term inference spend (we estimate ~20% extra token usage during the warmup window) and is causing your finance team to ask for a short-term mitigation.

To keep things moving, you asked whether Redwood can provide a one-time credit to offset the incremental cost tied specifically to the staggered rollout. Internally we discussed two pragmatic approaches:

- Conditional credit equal to estimated incremental spend (capped at $15k), reclaimed if full frontend rollout doesn't occur within the agreed window.
- A smaller, unconditional goodwill credit (~$7.5k) with no reclaim, to smooth procurement.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf) showing timelines and the frontend rollout checkpoint we propose (Target: 2027-08-10).

Can you confirm which option Procurement prefers? If you need a formal quote or a DocuSign, I can loop in Karthik for pricing and Laura for approval.

Thanks —
Tessa
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0123
attachments: mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmepay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmepay.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: one-time credit for staggered feature rollout (AcmePay)

Tessa —

Thanks for the quick note and for laying out options. Procurement prefers the conditional credit (option 1) — they want a clear checklist and a date by which the frontend must be live to avoid clawback. The $15k cap sounds reasonable as a starting point.

One question: can Redwood provide a short ledger showing how you estimated the 20% incremental spend (we need that for our internal approval)? Also, can we get a one-page amendment or order form that Procurement can sign this week?

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Head of Engineering, AcmePay
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: AcmePay conditional credit request — exec approval needed

Laura / Vanessa —

Looping you both in for a quick approval. AcmePay (large e-comm gateway) is asking for a conditional one-time credit capped at $15k to cover the incremental cost from a staggered embeddings rollout. They prefer a conditional credit (we reclaim if frontend not live by checkpoint). They requested a simple amendment / one-page order form this week.

Why I think we should approve:
- Customer is strategic for our payments vertical and onboarding is high visibility.
- Credit is limited ($15k cap) and tied to a clear win condition (frontend live by 2027-08-10).
- Approving removes a procurement blocker and accelerates committed usage (predictable revenue thereafter).

Proposed guardrails:
1) Credit applied as an invoice-level line item with clear expiry date.
2) If frontend not live by 2027-08-10, credit is reclaimed pro-rata for the months beyond the checkpoint.
3) Sign-off required from AcmePay on the included MAP document and a short ledger export we will provide.

If you want me to draft the amendment and the ledger, I can push that today. Requesting Laura for final executive sign-off.

—Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
attachments: SOW_AcmePay_v1.docx

Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AcmePay conditional credit request — exec approval needed

Thanks Karthik —

I approve the conditional one-time credit with the guardrails you’ve proposed. A few clarifications to bake into the amendment:

1) Define the observable we use to trigger reclaim (token spend delta vs baseline month, with a 10% noise buffer).
2) Credit must apply only to Redwood-hosted inference charges, not professional services or third-party infra.
3) Set an explicit 30-day window after 2027-08-10 for AcmePay to attest that the frontend rollout is complete (we will provide a simple checklist).

Karthik / Tessa: please send a one-page amendment (order form) and a short ledger export showing the incremental cost calc. Vanessa, help ops team flag the account for the credit line so billing can apply it cleanly. Monica, coordinate the checkout criteria with AcmePay.

Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
